✅ Mets — industry favorites, want long-term
⬇️ Dodgers — backing off, want shorter deal

Decision before the Dec. 1 lockout. 11 days. #Skubal #MLBHotStove

facebook.long_form:
The Skubal watch just got more interesting ⚾

Multiple sources now describe the New York Mets as the "industry favorites" to sign Tarik Skubal — the best starting pitcher on the free-agent market. The in-person meeting in Orange County reportedly "went very well," with the Mets sending a high-powered group including Steve Cohen and David Stearns to make their pitch directly to Skubal and his agent Scott Boras.

Meanwhile, the Dodgers appear to be fading from the race. Reports indicate the Dodgers want a shorter contract, while Skubal is seeking the long-term deal that would shatter the existing pitcher record (Yamamoto's 12yr/$325M). One publication links Skubal to a nine-year, $429 million scenario with New York.

The Blue Jays remain in the final group. Toronto has been aggressive this offseason and could make a final push if the Mets stall on terms.

The clock is the real variable here: the CBA expires December 1, and a lockout would freeze all free-agent transactions the following day. If Skubal doesn't sign in the next 11 days, he either signs before midnight December 1 or waits until spring. That's a complicated setup for a player with leverage.

The industry says New York. The contract math says historic. The timeline says now or wait.

**Caption Post**
Mets are the "industry favorites" to sign Tarik Skubal. Dodgers backing off. Blue Jays still in it. 11 days before the lockout freezes everything. ⚾ This gets resolved before December 1 or it doesn't get resolved at all.

stories.title: CBA Countdown — 11 Days, No Deal, Lockout Expected Dec. 2

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text:
MLB's CBA expires in 11 days (Dec. 1 at 11:59 PM ET).

Owners meetings in New York just ended. No deal reached. No progress.

The last lockout lasted 99 days. The 2027 season is at risk. #MLB #CBA

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
The core MLB lockout fight:

Owners want a salary cap and floor.
Players refuse any cap. Called it a "nonstarter."

Commissioner Manfred says no deal happens without both. Lockout expected Dec. 2. #MLB

facebook.long_form:
You have 11 days to watch major league free agency happen in real time ⏰

MLB's collective bargaining agreement expires December 1 at 11:59 PM Eastern. When it does, Commissioner Rob Manfred is expected to lock the players out within minutes — and every pending transaction in baseball freezes.

Here's what's at stake: Tarik Skubal (ace LHP, $325M–$429M projection), Seiya Suzuki (Japanese star, $110M projection), Teruaki Sato (NPB Triple Crown, $80M-$120M), Jazz Chisholm (elite infielder, $46M projection), Randy Arozarena (outfielder, $100M+ ask), and dozens of other free agents who have not yet signed.

What is the fight about? One thing: a salary cap. Owners want a cap and floor — a structure similar to the NBA and NFL. Commissioner Manfred has said MLB will not ratify a new CBA without both. The MLBPA has called a salary cap an absolute non-starter, arguing it would cost players roughly $400 million in earning potential annually.

The last MLB work stoppage (December 2021 to March 2022) lasted 99 days. The 2022 season lost its first two weeks. If this lockout follows the same pattern, spring training doesn't start until mid-March and the regular season begins late.

The informal deadline for 2027 games to be played is early March. That's the deadline no one wants to hit.

Watch the next 11 days very carefully. This is the most consequential window in baseball before the actual season.

**Caption Post**
11 days until the MLB lockout. Owners want a salary cap. Players refuse. December 1 is the wall. After that — Skubal, Suzuki, Sato, Chisholm, Arozarena, all frozen. ⏰ Baseball fans: watch this window closely.

---

stories.title: Suzuki to San Diego? Padres Emerge as Unlikely Frontrunner

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Jeff Passan reports: The Padres met with Seiya Suzuki and "could be the favorites" to sign him.

The Mariners are interested but won't do a long-term deal.

The Blue Jays are also pursuing Suzuki — while chasing Jazz Chisholm. #MLB #Padres

facebook.long_form:
Seiya Suzuki's free agency just got a plot twist 🌊

Jeff Passan reported that the San Diego Padres met with Suzuki and "could be the favorites" to sign him. This comes after weeks of speculation that pointed toward the Blue Jays or a return to Chicago. San Diego's interest is real, and their meeting apparently went well.

The Mariners, long considered a potential landing spot, are also interested — but are reportedly unlikely to offer the kind of long-term deal Suzuki is seeking. That's a significant development for Seattle, which needs outfield help but has a checkered history with high-dollar commitments.

Suzuki, who officially declined the Cubs' qualifying offer two weeks ago, is projected for approximately four years and $110 million by Spotrac. That puts him in a reasonable range for San Diego, which has been active in building around Manny Machado and Fernando Tatis Jr.

The complication: Toronto is also pursuing Suzuki while simultaneously chasing Jazz Chisholm. The Blue Jays have the resources for both but would likely need one to clear before committing to the other. If Chisholm signs first, Toronto pivots harder to Suzuki. If Suzuki signs first, they redirect to another outfield option.

Meanwhile, the Cubs are left with both Suzuki and Ian Happ as free agents, plus an entire starting rotation on the market. That's a significant rebuild under a December 1 deadline.

**Caption Post**
Jeff Passan: The Padres met with Seiya Suzuki and "could be the favorites" to sign him. 🌊 Mariners won't do long-term. Blue Jays chasing Suzuki AND Chisholm simultaneously. Cubs need a full roster rebuild in 11 days.

stories.title: Teruaki Sato's Dec. 16 Deadline — The One Big Signing Teams Can Do During a Lockout

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
Here's something most fans don't know:

Teruaki Sato can be signed DURING the MLB lockout.

Japanese NPB posting agreements exist outside the CBA framework. His Dec. 16 window stays open.

Teams that miss Skubal can still get Sato. #MLB #Sato

facebook.long_form:
Here's the most important thing most baseball fans don't know about the MLB offseason 🏮

Teruaki Sato can be signed during the MLB lockout.

Here's why: Sato's availability in the United States is governed by the NPB posting agreement — a separate international framework that exists entirely outside the MLB-MLBPA collective bargaining agreement. When the CBA expires December 1 and the lockout begins December 2, Sato's 45-day posting window (which opened November 1 and closes December 16) stays active. Teams can still negotiate with Sato and his representatives and sign him to a major league contract — even with the lockout in effect.

This is not a loophole in the pejorative sense — it's how the system is designed. Japanese posted players have always sat in a different legal category than domestic free agents. But the practical effect is significant: Sato becomes uniquely valuable for any team that misses out on Tarik Skubal.

Sato, 25, won the Japanese Central League Triple Crown in 2026, posting a .308 average with 39 home runs. Projections range from $80 million (Heyman's floor) to more than $120 million (Bowden). Teams linked: Mets, Yankees, Dodgers, Phillies.

The deadline is December 16. If Sato is unsigned by then, he returns to the Hanshin Tigers and cannot be posted again until next offseason. That's a one-year delay for every interested team.

The countdown is real. Watch for Sato news to accelerate over the next three weeks.

**Caption Post**
Teruaki Sato's posting window closes Dec. 16 — but here's the thing: he CAN be signed during the lockout. Japanese NPB posting agreements exist outside the CBA framework. Teams that miss Skubal get a second chance at a Triple Crown winner. 🏮 The window is 26 days. #MLB

stories.title: Randy Arozarena's $100M+ Ask is Stalling His Market

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
Randy Arozarena declined the qualifying offer and is asking for $100M-plus.

Suitors are balking (Passan). The Mariners won't do a long-term deal.

He has 11 days to get something done before the lockout freezes everything. #MLB

facebook.long_form:
Randy Arozarena is a genuinely excellent baseball player who may have overestimated his market 🤔

The two-way outfielder declined the qualifying offer earlier this month and hit free agency asking for well over $100 million, per Jeff Passan. The problem: suitors are balking. The Mariners — the team many expected to retain him after his 23-home-run, 41-steal season in Seattle — are reportedly unwilling to offer a long-term deal.

The numbers are interesting. Arozarena is 29 years old, a switch-hitter, plays solid left field, and has historically been one of the more exciting players in the sport. His 2026 slash line (.246/.328/.407) was down from his peak, and that may be contributing to market hesitancy. Add the qualifying offer compensation attached to his signing (the team that signs him loses a draft pick), and you have a player whose actual market value may be significantly below his ask.

The deadline pressure is real: the lockout on December 2 would freeze all transactions, meaning Arozarena has approximately 11 days to get a deal done or wait until spring to restart negotiations.

Teams like the Cubs (need an outfielder), Blue Jays (possibly, if they miss on Suzuki), and Orioles have been mentioned in connection with outfield needs. But none have made a public push for Arozarena at his asking price.

Something has to give — either Arozarena's ask comes down, or a team comes up to meet it. The clock is ticking.

**Caption Post**
Randy Arozarena wants $100M-plus. Suitors are balking (Passan). Mariners won't do long-term. He has 11 days before the lockout freezes his market. 🤔 Something has to give — and it's usually the player's ask.
